questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
options: मैं सो रहा था और फिर मैं सो रहा था
questions.explanation_en: The bare stem comes first and the marker second. Reversing them separates the verb from its own ending.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: -ऊँगा belongs to मैं. In the future the ending identifies the person, so the wrong ending names the wrong person.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: Both agreeing words go plural. In this cell you can hear the mismatch, because रहा and थे do not rhyme.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: There is only ever one auxiliary. The past replaces the present one rather than being added behind it.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: तुम is grammatically plural whatever the past tense is doing, so both agreeing words stay plural.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The long ी cannot take -ों directly. It shortens to ि and a य appears between the vowels.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: Two errors at once: भाई must shorten its vowel, and बहन has no vowel for a य to bridge.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: A postposition forces the oblique form, and बेटा changes to बेटे.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is the grammatically correct sentence/phrase?
questions.explanation_en: The claim is about cities in general, so the plural oblique शहरों is needed.
